scenes.visual: Title card: The Test: Silence the STN.

scenes.tts: If dopamine loss makes the S T N overactive, what happens when you silence it?
scenes.caption: If dopamine loss makes the STN overactive, what happens when you silence it?
scenes.visual: The box column from chapter two after dopamine loss: STN bright, GPi's foot pressing down. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: If dopamine loss makes the STN overactive, what happens when you silence it?

scenes.tts: Picture a monkey made parkinsonian with M P T P, a toxin that kills dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra.
scenes.caption: Picture a monkey made parkinsonian with MPTP, a toxin that kills dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra.
scenes.visual: A schematic, non-photographic monkey outline. Beside it, the SNc box fades. Label: MPTP.
scenes.narration: Picture a monkey made parkinsonian with MPTP, a toxin that kills dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra.

scenes.tts: Now lesion its left S T N. Which way should movement change? And on which side of the body?
scenes.caption: Now lesion its left STN. Which way should movement change? And on which side of the body?
scenes.visual: The left STN is marked with a lesion symbol. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Now lesion its left STN. Which way should movement change? And on which side of the body?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; the left STN stays marked.

scenes.tts: Start with the sign. The S T N excites the brake, and the brake inhibits the thalamus. That is one inhibition, an odd number.
scenes.caption: Start with the sign. The STN excites the brake, and the brake inhibits the thalamus. That is one inhibition, an odd number.
scenes.visual: The STN to GPi arrow (plus chip) and the GPi to thalamus arrow (minus chip) light up. Label: 1 flip, odd.
scenes.narration: Start with the sign. The STN excites the brake, and the brake inhibits the thalamus. That is one inhibition, an odd number.

scenes.tts: So when S T N activity falls, the thalamus rises. The brake lifts, toward movement.
scenes.caption: So when STN activity falls, the thalamus rises. The brake lifts, toward movement.
scenes.visual: STN ticks stop; GPi slows; the foot lifts; the thalamus brightens.
scenes.narration: So when STN activity falls, the thalamus rises. The brake lifts, toward movement.

scenes.tts: Now the side. In the classic model, the left loop returns to the left cortex.
scenes.visual: A frontal outline: the loop from left STN through left GPi and left thalamus to left cortex glows, staying on the left.
scenes.narration: Now the side. In the classic model, the left loop returns to the left cortex.

scenes.tts: Its commands then cross once, at the pyramidal decussation. So the change should appear on the right side.
scenes.visual: The corticospinal line from chapter one runs from left cortex through the X to the right arm and leg, which brighten.
scenes.narration: Its commands then cross once, at the pyramidal decussation. So the change should appear on the right side.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety, Bergman, Wichmann and DeLong did this experiment in monkeys treated with M P T P.
scenes.caption: In 1990, Bergman, Wichmann and DeLong did this experiment in monkeys treated with MPTP.
scenes.visual: Text on screen: Bergman, Wichmann and DeLong, Science, 1990. The monkey outline returns with the left STN removed.
scenes.narration: In 1990, Bergman, Wichmann and DeLong did this experiment in monkeys treated with MPTP.

scenes.tts: The parkinsonian signs improved on the side of the body opposite the lesion.
scenes.visual: A schematic movement trace for the right arm recovers, labelled schematic. Label: opposite side improved.
scenes.narration: The parkinsonian signs improved on the side of the body opposite the lesion.

scenes.tts: The prediction held. This work helped make the S T N a target for Parkinson's surgery, and for deep brain stimulation.
scenes.caption: The prediction held. This work helped make the STN a target for Parkinson's surgery, and for deep brain stimulation.
scenes.visual: A check mark beside the prediction card. A target ring appears over the STN, then a schematic electrode descends to it. Label: deep brain stimulation.
scenes.narration: The prediction held. This work helped make the STN a target for Parkinson's surgery, and for deep brain stimulation.

scenes.tts: But the count has a hard limit. In mice, both pathways become active together around the start of an action.
scenes.visual: Split panel: two schematic calcium traces, direct and indirect, both rising at action onset. Label: schematic, after Cui and colleagues, 2013.
scenes.narration: But the count has a hard limit. In mice, both pathways become active together around the start of an action.

scenes.tts: When two routes pull in opposite directions, counting cannot say which one wins. That depends on how strong each route is.
scenes.visual: Two arrows pull on GPi in opposite directions. Label: opposite signs, the count makes no call.
scenes.narration: When two routes pull in opposite directions, counting cannot say which one wins. That depends on how strong each route is.

scenes.tts: The model also gives no account of rest tremor. And how deep brain stimulation works is still unresolved.
scenes.visual: Two open-question cards: rest tremor; how deep brain stimulation works.
scenes.narration: The model also gives no account of rest tremor. And how deep brain stimulation works is still unresolved.

scenes.tts: Count crossings for side and inhibitions for sign. Then check the count against the data.
scenes.visual: End card line: Count crossings for side, inhibitions for sign. Then check against the data.
scenes.narration: Count crossings for side and inhibitions for sign. Then check the count against the data.
